independent_review.text:
# Independent review: option disabled signal v2

The bounded v2 change is supported subject to a fresh current-tree source comparison, separate review of the new `signal` authored use, and normal integration checks. This supersedes the v1 nonadmission for its specific `_disabledState` subclass collision; it does not grant a full compatibility or release pass. Frozen patch SHA256 `ee906cc31a2c9aed436285b3ec2833f5054083203e66dd7e2521893d2716ad18`; validation `ad485637779a0cadcec16ff94b7f8d6ce3305eb5d0f53983fb8598153bbe7b2e`; README `0c6e5b78e5843941c91f051e5819570b9e8c3fd60217515d28137c2dba96c59b`; validator `ce9356b2bdfd7dab503a6a01fc9ee6a1f84a3e10e6e274c7c144797cc60ec99c`. The earlier v1 review and its concrete counterexample remain archived.

V2 retains the existing private TypeScript `_disabled` own boolean and public coercing setter/group-or-local getter, and tracks the getter via a distinct ECMAScript private signal `#legacyDisabledState`. The emitted declaration adds an unnamed `#private` slot instead of a named TypeScript-private `_disabledState`. Independently compiled nine controls against actual extracted baseline, v1 and v2: consumer subclass fields named `_disabledState` as private or public compile on baseline and v2 but fail on v1 with TS2415; an independent child `#legacyDisabledState` compiles on all three. The independently rerun result is `subclass-replay.json` SHA256 `5f8c3e1ef86bf758a5cabc08568787714c5130230b653bcac3d562d0256b7c62`. Independent manual runtime controls show baseline and v2 agree on getter/setter booleans and retain the child's public value and own boolean field; the v1 public-field subclass throws. The child ECMAScript-private field also remains independent. These are focused controls, not proof of all subclass, proxy or reflection behavior; direct private `_disabled` mutation remains outside the notification setter.

Independently reran the bounded validator to an isolated file: its complete output exactly matches validation SHA256 `ad485637779a0cadcec16ff94b7f8d6ce3305eb5d0f53983fb8598153bbe7b2e`. Both exact 512-member archives and their extracted consumers, source maps, equal AOT fixture/compiled output, no Zone.js/runtime-compiler bundle inputs, retained family reports and the readiness/notification mutants pass its bounded checks. I also compared the complete archives: only legacy-core FESM, FESM map, declaration and declaration map differ. V2 packed tar is SHA256 `06d53f7b54724b92424ca712977db354e79eb6b6e004c99036bd91eb71cfe147`; its baseline is `2cf96975b6f6adaa83a8bf42f99a756f34bbdd7166ea899120f5605c66f8bffb`.

Independently reran the existing AOT fixture in Chromium 149, with the same extracted v2 pack, in dev and production. Both passed both stale-parent checks with `typeof Zone === 'undefined'`; independent raw reports are `aot/results.json` SHA256 `05f2df448f3cba57c5b184e76c382426729adba1abb556fb4666bfc5f1584fef` and `aot/production-results.json` SHA256 `6c3debd4a9990d31fa81a4cda7d92d6fb2454d71f9c98a8add0e2bf49e30c3bd`. They exercise true→false and false→true stable rendering, unrelated click, disabled selection and early/dynamic selection path. The retained baseline fails both parent checks; the retained notification-deleted unpacked mutant does too. The retained separate readiness mutant is not a packed artifact. Maintained TestBed selected reports are baseline select 292/293 with NG0100, candidate 293/293 and core 32/32, with Zone.js present. The standalone AOT generic NG0100 positive control did not pass, so no generic changed-after-check coverage is claimed.

The original 16 source was inspected, not run in this no-Zone scenario. The fixture uses pinned installed 22.1.7 peers through symlinks, not a clean-install floor test. No new HTML/CSS/Sass or consumer API mirror is introduced. No full historical inventory, cross-browser, x64, 21.x, security, G11 or release qualification follows.
